title: Apostate canonical launch configuration
description: The normalized launch contract shared by the CLI, Python package, and Node package. Profile selection precedence is explicit profile file > inline profile object > fingerprint seed plus platform persona > persisted seed for this user-data-dir > a newly drawn seed, persisted. Network localization precedence is explicit locale/timezone > GeoIP-derived locale/timezone > composed locale/timezone > host values. A launch resolves this configuration once before the browser process starts; adapters must not add per-call randomness and must not log proxy credentials. Composition itself runs in the browser process and is not reimplemented by an adapter (docs/concepts/how-it-works.mdx).

fingerprint.description: A deterministic profile selector. It may be a non-negative integer, a non-empty stable seed string, or the literal "host" to request host inheritance. Null requests the default: a seed drawn once from OS entropy and persisted to <user-data-dir>/apostate/seed, then reused for every later launch against the same directory. Integer seeds are bounded to remain exact in JavaScript and JSON number implementations; string seeds are normalized as opaque identifiers and must not contain credentials or whitespace.

fingerprint_platform.description: The platform persona used with fingerprint. Opt-in: null uses the host's own platform as the persona. It selects OS identity, client hints, fonts, voices, locale, screen geometry and hardware buckets, and it does not move the GPU capability cluster, which is chosen from the anchors the host's graphics backend can serve. A persona that disagrees with the resolved anchor is reported as a limitation rather than hidden. This is a persona name, not the release artifact target; release targets are recorded in release/manifest.schema.json.

profile.description: An explicit profile file path or inline device-profile object. A non-null value takes precedence over seed composition and bypasses it entirely, so its coherence and servability are the author's responsibility. Inline objects must validate against the public device-profile schema. Catalogue profile IDs are not accepted: catalogue version 2 composes profiles from anchors and dispersion axes instead of offering a fixed list of families.

locale.description: An explicit BCP 47 locale tag. When non-null it wins over GeoIP and the composed locale; null allows the network/composed/host precedence chain.

timezone.description: An explicit IANA-style timezone name (or UTC/GMT). When non-null it wins over GeoIP and the composed timezone; null allows the network/composed/host precedence chain.

geoip.description: Resolve the observed network exit before launch and use its location for locale/timezone only when those values were not explicitly supplied. A failed lookup must be reported rather than silently inventing values. Geography never selects device traits.

proxy.description: An opaque HTTP(S), SOCKS4, or SOCKS5 proxy URI. Userinfo is accepted for authenticated proxies and must be kept in memory only: adapters and diagnostics must redact it and must never emit it in logs or manifests.

headless.description: Whether to start Chromium in headless mode.

user_data_dir.description: Persistent user-data directory path. It is also the seed's lifetime: the default seed is persisted here, so a persistent directory yields a stable identity and an ephemeral one yields a new identity per launch. Null requests an adapter-managed temporary profile.

args.description: Additional Chromium command-line arguments. Arguments are opaque to this contract; adapters must avoid logging values that can contain proxy credentials or other secrets.
